The purpose of the Model HR Policy is to align with the Ministry of Cooperation’s vision of “Sahakar
se Samriddhi”, aiming to bring uniformity, transparency, and professionalism in HR management
across Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) / Large Area Multipurpose Society (LAMPS) /
The objective of the HR Policy is to:
• Establish uniform staffing norms and recruitment systems aligned with PACS/LAMPS/FSS
• Ensure merit-based hiring and continuous capacity building for diversified service delivery.
• Promote professional ethics, regulatory compliance, and cooperative values across all levels.
• Implement structured appraisals and incentive mechanisms to reward performance and
• Develop a digitally competent, compliance -oriented workforce integrated with national
• Enhance employee dignity, welfare, and career progression through clear roles and service
• Encourage inclusive, transparent, and accountable workplace practices to boost motivation
• Overall, provide a strategic framework to address ad -hoc staffing, skill deficits, and low
accountability, ensuring efficiency, good governance, and long -term sustainability of PACS
● Ensure that qualification, selection, and performance norms for PACS HR are non-negotiable
and uniformly upheld across all States/UTs, with no compromise on merit-based standards.
● Formulate the policy in active consultation with PACS Employee Federations and
States/UTs, ensuring grassroots legitimacy and ownership of the HR framework.
● Cater to the special needs of Northeastern States covered under the 5th and 6th Schedules of
the Indian Constitution, with appropriate flexibility in implementation while maintaining
To help apply the Model HR Policy in a standardized and practical way, PACS/LAMPS/FSS are
classified into categories A+ to F based on audited business levels from the previous financial year.
These levels include loans, deposits, mini-bank turnover, and other non-credit activities.

This classification allows flexible and scalable staffing aligned with each PACS/LAMPS/FSS’s size
and growth. A categorization matrix defines the suggested staff strength and roles for each category.

The DLPAF shall support PACS/LAMPS/FSS under financial stress or facing consistent losses,
ensuring weak but potentially viable societies are not left out of reforms due to lack of resources.
Support to be provided through a need-based and tapering financial model, helping PACS implement
Business Development Plans (BDPs) and move toward operational stability.
DLPAF involves key stakeholders — StCB, DCCBs, and the State Government — to build a
4.1.1 Contributions as per Financial Health of StCB and DCCBs
• Both StCB & DCCB are in overall profit: 50% each by StCB and DCCB.
• StCB in profit, DCCB in loss: Split equally between StCB and State Govt.
• StCB in loss, DCCB with profit (despite accumulated loss): Equal contributions by StCB,
• Both StCB & DCCB in loss: Fully supported by State Govt.
A Potentially Viable PACS refers to a PACS that, although not currently profitable, demonstrates the
structural capacity, member base, business potential, and operational intent to achieve financial self-
sufficiency within a defined time frame — typically 3 to 5 years. Key attributes include:
• Basic Infrastructure: Own or functional premises, digital readiness (‘ePACS Only’ under
• Governance Structure: Elected Board and functioning management committee, audit
compliance in progress or achievable with support.
• Operational Base: Active membership, access to finance from higher tier, and willingness to
• Location Advantage: Situated in a rural or semi -rural area with demand for agri -inputs,
credit, PDS, CSC, or other services.
• Growth Willingness: Demonstrates readiness to participate in institutional strengthening
through BDP duly approved by the DLPC.
4.3 Provision for Access to Tapered Funding
Interest-free or soft loans may be extended to PACS/LAMPS/FSS through DLPAF to support HR -
related expenses, particularly salaries and operational costs, on a tapering basis.

SLPAF combines State and StCB funds to support PACS in 2 -tier structure. If the StCB is in profit,

supported by State/UT government. Neither MoC nor NABARD shall contribute to SLPAF.

6.2 Compliance Norms for Existing Staff at PACS/LAMPS/FSS
All currently serving Secretaries and Assistant Executives who do not meet the prescribed minimum
qualifications and have more than 10 years of service remaining shall be required to acquire the
stipulated qualifications within maximum five years from the date of implementation of this HR
Policy (degrees in 3 years, diploma in 2 years). Secretary/Manager/Accountant/AE shall be trained
within 15 days on all ePACS software modules post announcement of ‘ePACS Only’.
6.3 Provision for Transition of Charge in Case of Vacancy of Secretary
In case of retirement, resignation, or any unexpected vacancy of the Secretary, a smooth and clear
handover must be ensured. The Board of the PACS, in consultation with the
DLPC/SLPC/representative of RCS, shall proactively make arrangements for charge handover. This
may involve appointment of an interim or acting Secretary, in no case exceeding 3 months, during
which period regular recruitment should be effected.

The list of selected or wait -listed candidates, empanelled through the recruitment process, shall

16.2 Periodic Review of HR Policy by Committee Constituted by MoC
The PACS HR Policy shall be treated as a dynamic and evolving framework, subject to regular review.
The Committee constituted by the Ministry of Cooperation (MoC) shall undertake a comprehensive
review every five years. States may conduct interim reviews a t periodic intervals based on local
requirements and evolving operational dynamics. Reviews shall aim to:

• Promote best practices in human resource management.
The Northeastern States of India — comprising Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya,
Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura — present a unique cooperative landscape characterised
by tribal land ownership patterns, dispersed populations, remote geogr aphy, multi -lingual
communities, and areas governed under the 5th and 6th Schedules of the Indian Constitution.
● The 6th Schedule of the Indian Constitution (Articles 244(2) and 275(1)) provides for
autonomous district councils in the tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram,
with powers to make regulations on management of institutions and cooperative societies.
● The 5th Schedule (Article 244(1)) applies to scheduled areas in other states and empowers
Governors to make regulations on cooperative activities in tribal areas.
● PACS operating within 5th and 6th Schedule areas may be subject to regulations enacted by
Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) that supplement or modify State cooperative law.
● This HR Policy shall apply to all PACS in NE States subject to applicable ADC regulations;
where any provision of this Policy conflicts with a valid ADC regulation, the matter shall be
referred to the concerned State Government for resolution.
